steps.text: Begin with the branch, so the bird sits in front of it. Outline both branches with split stitch in 738, then fill the pale sunlit wood with long and short stitch, running your rows lengthways along the grain. Blend in 3045 for the mid-tone and 830 for the shaded underside, then use the darkest 838 in the deepest hollows. Finish with a scatter of 830 and 838 french knots for the bark speckles.

Outline the leaf with split stitch in 524 and fill the lit half, angling your rows outward from the central vein to the edge. Blend 3013 into the shaded half, and lay a line of split stitch in 3013 down the middle for the vein.

Now the tail. Work in 3799, letting the feathers radiate from the tail base out to the tips - keep every row travelling in that fan direction. Mark the divisions between the long feathers with fine split-stitch lines in 3371 so they read as separate feathers, not one grey mass.
Fill the small dark shadow where the tail meets the back with 838, tucking short rows underneath the wing. This deep tone sets off the bright rump that comes next.
Fill the vivid orange rump patch with 741, following the curve of the back. A touch of 830 along its upper edge keeps it from floating.

Outline the black mantle with split stitch in 3371, then fill it with long and short stitch flowing from the neck back towards the tail. Blend a little 3799 along the lower edge where the black meets the grey wing, so the two don't sit as hard blocks.

Fill the folded wing with 3799, sweeping your rows from the shoulder down and back towards the wing tip. Lay fine split-stitch lines in 3371 along each flight feather - these thin directional lines are what make the wing look layered and real rather than flat.

Work the soft grey-green wing coverts in 926, as small overlapping feathers stepping down towards the belly. Blend a hint of 798 in at the top so they sit quietly between the grey wing and the blue head.
Fill the orange flank patch low on the side with 741, curving the rows with the side of the breast and blending down into where the yellow belly will go.
Fill the breast and belly with 729, working rows that curve down and around the breast from the throat to the feet. Let it blend up into the 741 flank so the orange melts into the gold.

Outline the head with split stitch in 798 and fill it with stitches radiating outward from around the eye - short rows over the crown, longer ones sweeping down to the throat. Blend a little 926 at the lower cheek so the head joins the body softly.

Finally, the face. Satin-stitch the beak in 3371 from base to tip, and lay the short dark lore line from the eye towards the beak. Work the eye as a single french knot of 3371 set inside a tiny ring of 535 - that bright ring gives your tanager its watchful gaze. Your Darwin's Tanager is finished!
